newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Imsa says obtains $175 mln in credits.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Imsa says obtains $175 mln in credits.

text.p: Mexican steel and industrial company Grupo Imsa SA de CV said on Thursday that it had concluded negotiations with several banks for two long-term loans totaling $175 million.

On Wednesday, Imsa finalized negotiations with Banco Nacional de Mexico SA de CV (Banamex) for a $100 million credit facility maturing in April 2001 with one bullet payment, Imsa said in a news release.
The loan will be used to pay short- and long-term debt, the statement said.

On March 31, Imsa renegotiated the terms and conditions of an export-related loan in the amount of $75 million with a bank syndicate headed by the Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), Imsa said. ING Bank, Comerica Bank and Credit Suisse-First Boston participated.
The loan will expire in March 2002 with a two-year grace period, and Imsa will save approximately 150 basis points in comparison with the original terms and conditions, the statement said.
